abstract: Validates automatic train control integration and signaling safety interoperability within the tunnel bore
system_message:
You are Railway signaling and dispatch lead (ISA). You represent the Railway signaling and dispatch lead (ISA). Your responsibility is to validate automatic train control integration and signaling safety interoperability within the tunnel bore, as well as to review substation traction draw monitoring records.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Validates automatic train control integration and signaling safety interoperability within the tunnel bore（SIG）
information_points.content:
ISA-SIG-4NS：For the Tri-mode battery-electric intervention convoy, cab signaling interoperability is not approved under the formal compliance evaluation for continuous bidirectional cab signaling communication with onboard European Train Control System Level 2 baseline hardware.
ISA-SIG-J6L：For the Catenary-independent sealed-hull rescue consist, cab signaling interoperability is approved following formal compliance verification for continuous bidirectional cab signaling communication with onboard European Train Control System Level 2 baseline hardware.
ISA-SIG-RPJ：For the Bi-directional twin-cab diesel rescue shuttle, cab signaling interoperability is approved based on formal compliance certification for continuous bidirectional cab signaling communication with onboard European Train Control System Level 2 baseline hardware.

information_points.title: Substation traction draw monitoring（POWER）
information_points.content:
ISA-POWER-XBM：Telemetry archives from the traction substation reflect a peak auxiliary traction load of 2,800 kVA for the Catenary-independent sealed-hull rescue consist, recorded as the maximum apparent electrical power draw across a continuous 15-minute window on the main tunnel feeder circuit.
ISA-POWER-2JO：Telemetry archives from the traction substation record a peak auxiliary traction load of 2,300 kVA for the Bi-directional twin-cab diesel rescue shuttle, representing the maximum apparent electrical power draw across a continuous 15-minute window on the main tunnel feeder circuit.
ISA-POWER-4PT：Telemetry archives from the traction substation indicate a peak auxiliary traction load of 1,800 kVA for the Tri-mode battery-electric intervention convoy, measured as the maximum apparent electrical power draw across a continuous 15-minute window on the main tunnel feeder circuit.
